SUMMARY: Senior buyer role in Ledgerline responsible for monthly certificate-expiry monitoring and supplier notifications for UN 38.3 compliance.
INFOBOX:
Role code: PUR-SR
Role title: Senior Buyer
Status: current
Effective date: 2026-09-01
Owner: Purchase Department
System: Ledgerline
CONFLICTS:
- none
BODY:
Role PUR-SR corresponds to the senior buyer within Ledgerline and the purchase team. Under current operating amendments, the role carries specific recurring compliance responsibilities for battery certificate management across active vendors[^r1].

## Responsibilities

The senior buyer is required to run the certificate-expiry report per MAN-PUR-72 §22.6 on the first working day of every month with a 90-day window[^r1]. Using this report, the role holder must notify suppliers that have expiring [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]][^r1].

SUMMARY: Purchasing rules and compliance requirements for the BAT-* lithium battery components family.
INFOBOX:
Code Prefix: BAT-
Family: Battery components
Status: Current
CONFLICTS:
- none
BODY:
The `BAT-*` item family encompasses battery components, including lithium battery items used across Northbridge Cycles' product lines. When raising purchase orders for lithium battery components under this family, specific certification checks must be verified prior to order placement [^r1].

## Purchasing requirements

Raising purchase orders for lithium battery components requires verifying that the [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] was issued within 12 months and remains valid for at least 60 days post-order placement [^r1]. These mandatory checks for purchasing staff are established under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]] [^r1].

SUMMARY: Supplier policy governing supplier compliance, including certificate validity requirements for battery items.
INFOBOX:
Code: POL-SUP-003
Type: policy
Status: current
Effective date: 2026-09-01
Owner: Purchasing
CONFLICTS:
- superseded | UN 38.3 certificates must be issued within the last 12 months with valid-to at least 60 days beyond PO placement date | Older 24-month validity rule allowed longer validity before 1 September 2026 | r1,r2
BODY:
POL-SUP-003 sets out the standards and compliance requirements for Northbridge Cycles' suppliers. As of 1 September 2026, the policy incorporates amended compliance standards for battery certifications under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]]. Any purchase order placed today requires strict adherence to updated validity windows for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] covering [[items-bat|BAT-* items]].

## Clauses

### 4.4 Battery certification compliance
Effective 1 September 2026 via [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], UN 38.3 certificates must be issued within the last 12 months and maintain a valid-to date at least 60 days beyond the purchase order placement date [^r1]. Battery certificates issued under the older 24-month validity rule are treated as having no certificate for any orders placed on or after 1 September 2026 [^r2].

## Versions and conflicts

UN 38.3 certificates verify transport safety testing for lithium-cell parts across [[items-bat|BAT-* items]][^r1]. Under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], Northbridge Cycles enforces strict issuance and validity windows prior to raising purchase orders[^r1]. Active compliance is tracked monthly by purchasing staff to ensure supplier documentation does not lapse during procurement cycles[^r2].

## Acceptance Criteria

Since 1 September 2026 under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell parts are only accepted if issued within the preceding 12 months with a validity extending at least 60 days past order date[^r1].

## Monitoring and Compliance

The [[role-pur-sr|senior buyer]] executes the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) on the first working day of each month using a 90-day threshold to notify suppliers of impending UN 38.3 expirations[^r2].

INFOBOX:

---
title: AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy
type: policy
slug: amd-sup-2026-02
summary: Replaces POL-SUP-003 §4.4 from 1 September 2026, requiring UN 38.3 certificates issued within 12 months with a 60-day expiry buffer.
audience: staff
sources:
  - AMD-SUP-2026-02 v1.0
status: current
created: 2026-08-14
updated: 2026-09-01
---
AMD-SUP-2026-02 is an amendment to [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] that tightened the acceptance criteria for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] on 1 September 2026 [^r1][^r2]. It requires test certificates for lithium-cell orders to be issued within the preceding 12 months and carry a validity buffer of at least 60 days past the order date [^r2]. As of 26 October 2026, this rule is in full effect across all new purchase orders for [[items-bat|BAT-* items]] [^r2][^r3].

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document code | AMD-SUP-2026-02 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Author | L. Moreno |
| Owner | Purchase |
| Effective date | 2026-09-01 |
| Status | Current |
| Amends | POL-SUP-003 §4.4 |

## Clauses

### 1. What changes
With effect from 1 September 2026, POL-SUP-003 §4.4 is replaced so that a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order placement date [^r2]. Certificates meeting the former rule of being issued within 24 months and unexpired count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, while orders released before that date remain unaffected [^r3].

### 2. Why
The policy amendment was introduced because a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed Northbridge's incoming abuse test in July 2026 after the underlying cell maker changed [^r4].

### 3. What purchase staff must do
Purchase staff must inspect the certificate's issue date and valid-to date against the new 12-month issuance and 60-day expiry buffer rule before raising an order for a lithium-cell part [^r5]. The [[role-pur-sr|senior buyer]] must run the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) on the first working day of each month with a 90-day window and contact every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate expires within that window [^r6]. All provisions of POL-SUP-003 §4 other than §4.4 remain in full effect [^r7].

## Versions and conflicts
- Today's rule (effective 2026-09-01): A UN 38.3 certificate must be issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date must be at least 60 days after the purchase order placement date [^r2].
- Superseded rule: A UN 38.3 certificate was accepted if issued within 24 months and unexpired [^r3].
- Sources and dates: POL-SUP-003 §4.4 superseded on 2026-09-01 by AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1 [^r2][^r3].
- Kind: superseded.
